title: A reduced singleton stack with quasi-compact diagonal is a gerbe over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $\mathcal C$ be an algebraic stack over $k$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Suppose $\mathcal C$ is reduced, meaning that it admits a smooth surjective scheme atlas all of whose local rings have no nonzero nilpotents. Suppose the field-valued point space $|\mathcal C|$ of [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets] has exactly one point, and the diagonal $\mathcal C\to\mathcal C\times_k\mathcal C$ is quasi-compact [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. There exist a field extension $L/k$ and a $k$-morphism $p:\mathcal C\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] which is a gerbe: for each scheme $T\to\operatorname{Spec}L$, the fibre groupoid has objects fppf locally on $T$, and any two such objects are isomorphic fppf locally on $T$ [def-pc-fppf-site]. No local Noetherianity or local finite-type hypothesis on $\mathcal C/k$, and no algebraicity or finiteness hypothesis on $L/k$, is imposed.

source.place: Tag 06RC, proposition-open-stratum, applied to a reduced singleton stack (its inertia is a base change of its quasi-compact diagonal); Tag 0DQL, lemma-gerbe-diagonal-quasi-compact. The quotient algebraic space is reduced by spaces-descent.tex Tag 0GB3, lemma-reduced-local-smooth, and a field spectrum by decent-spaces.tex Tag 047Z, lemma-when-field; quasi-separated spaces are decent by decent-spaces.tex Tag 03JX, lemma-bounded-fibres and the decency conditions.

proof.text: Write $I=I_{\mathcal C/k}$. The definition [def-sfb-moduli-inertia] identifies $I$ with $\mathcal C\times_{\mathcal C\times_k\mathcal C}\mathcal C$, where both maps are the diagonal: a pair of objects with two isomorphisms is equivalent to one object with their ratio as automorphism. Thus $I\to\mathcal C$ is a base change of the given quasi-compact diagonal. Quasi-compactness is stable under base change directly from [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]: each quasi-compact test of the new target is the same test of the old target after composition, and the two fibre products agree.

source.place: Tag 050P (lemma-diagonal-diagonal), explicit inertia square; Tag 050U, definition-quasi-compact

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-qc-inertia-dense-open-gerbe] to the reduced stack $\mathcal C$ and the inertia projection of step 1. Obtain a dense open substack $\mathcal U$ and a gerbe $\mathcal U\to Q$ over an algebraic space $Q/k$. The nonempty singleton $|\mathcal C|$ has no proper dense open subset, so $|\mathcal U|=|\mathcal C|$. An open immersion with full point image is an equivalence: after every scheme test its open subscheme has all points, using surjectivity of points of stack fibre products [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets], and hence is the whole scheme. Thus the gerbe is $p:\mathcal C\to Q$.

By [lem-sfb-gerbe-smooth-universal-homeomorphism], $p$ is smooth and induces a homeomorphism $|\mathcal C|\to|Q|$, so $|Q|$ is a nonempty singleton. Choose the reduced smooth surjective scheme atlas $V\to\mathcal C$ in the hypothesis. The smoothness assertion of that node, tested on this atlas, makes $V\to Q$ smooth and surjective. Since $V$ is reduced, [lem-sfb-space-smooth-reduced-locality] implies that $Q$ is reduced. Apply [lem-sfb-gerbe-qc-diagonal-descent] to $p$; the diagonal of $Q/k$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Tags 06R9 and 0DN8 (gerbe homeomorphism and smoothness), 0DQL; spaces-descent.tex Tag 0GB3

proof.text: Let $q$ be the unique point of $Q$. By [lem-sfb-qs-space-field-monomorphism], its quasi-compact diagonal supplies a field $L$ and a quasi-compact monomorphism $j:\operatorname{Spec}L\to Q$ over $k$. Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-singleton-field-factorization] with $X=Y=Q$ and $f=\mathrm{id}_Q$; the reducedness and point-image hypotheses hold by step 3. Obtain $g:Q\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ over $k$ with $jg=\mathrm{id}_Q$. Since $j(gj)=j$, the monomorphism property gives $gj=\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{Spec}L}$. Hence $Q\simeq\operatorname{Spec}L$ over $k$. Its structure map makes $L$ a field extension of $k$ (a unital map between fields is injective). Compose $p$ with $g$. Under the inverse maps $j,g$, the fibre groupoids over each scheme are the same, so both fppf gerbe conditions for $p$ give those for $gp$. No finite-type property of $L/k$ has been used.
